b_stack_watermark.primed_range: Stack::usable_start() .. Stack::top, i.e. [base + guard_pages*4096, top) with guard_pages = STACK_GUARD_PAGES = 2 (the 2 bottom guard frames are unmapped and NOT primed); length = usable_bytes = pages*4096. Both the kernel stack and the user stack of each task (user pages are USER|RW identity-mapped; x86 has no SMAP/SMEP code in hal/arch/x86 or kernel so the CPL0 write to user pages is legal).
b_stack_watermark.scan: Stack::test_hook_watermark_bytes = usable - (length of the leading run of 0xA5 starting at usable_start); an idle stack reads the trap frame (kernel: ViTrapFrame at top, task.rs:179) as used; a legitimately written 0xA5 byte can only under-count.

c_stack_baseline_emission.boot_phase: maybe_emit_boot_stack_baselines (task.rs:729-764), called from the timer-tick ISR (task.rs:1026-1027) on every tick of both harts once system_ticks()>=1500 (hart 0 counts ticks). For each task whose name is in {init, cellbox [b2: shell], vfs, net, virtio-net, thread} (vfs-test deferred) not yet emitted: emits kind=kernel then kind=user, phase=boot, ONCE per name (STACK_BASELINE_EMITTED bit). It is a first-seen-after-tick-1500 sample, NOT a post-workload watermark. Workers (ls/cat/echo/ps/kill), terminal, compositor etc. NEVER emit.
c_stack_baseline_emission.consequence: Final per-task watermarks (cellbox user/kernel at end of workload, workers, terminal) cannot come from the guest [stack-baseline] lines; they must be read from guest memory by host introspection of the primed 0xA5 stacks (scan from usable_start for the first non-0xA5 byte) while the task is alive; a worker stack is freed at exit (frames return to the allocator with their contents until reuse).

reproduction_controls.note: The non-hooks control kernel built by the same driver in the disposable trees is byte-identical to the previously qualified/built kernel in all four profiles, so the recipe, paths and toolchain are proven equal; the only difference between control and measurement kernel is the `test-hooks` cargo feature.

validity_assessment: No hook found that changes the behaviour of cellbox/shell/ls/cat/echo/ps/kill/terminal workloads other than stack fill pattern (0xA5), per-spawn memset and per-tick scheduler-lock scan, so the comparison is not invalidated by a forced behaviour change; STOPPED was therefore not used. The measurement kernel is a different binary from the qualified kernel, boots a large pre-init selftest corpus, and carries boot-fatal asserts that have not run against the canonical images: a single (D7-3) run can end in a boot panic that is not a workload result. Main/the user should decide whether to accept that risk before the run.
